transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. Before we get started, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Yeah, hi. Um, well, I guess I'm here because... well, it's work stuff mostly. I'm a wholesale buyer, and lately it's just been a lot. Actually, did you know how much markup there is on basic athletic socks? It's insane, we get them for literal pennies from overseas and retail them for like fifteen bucks a pack. I was looking at the pallets in the warehouse the other day and just thinking about all that cotton and how much space it takes up, and the dust it leaves everywhere. 

But anyway, sorry, what really made me come in is that I just can't shake this feeling that people at work—and even some of the vendors we buy from—are tracking my buys behind my back. Like, I know they're purposely messing with the launch numbers to make me look stupid. My supervisor sat me down and showed me the reports, and she says they don't prove anything is going on, but... I don't know, I just know what's happening.
How long have you been feeling this way about your coworkers and vendors tracking or sabotaging your work—days, weeks, or longer?

Um, well, it's been... I'd say roughly ten months now. Yeah, about ten months of the suspicious stuff, and... and the voice, too. It all started right around the time we switched our main supplier for the poly-blend t-shirts. 

Which, by the way, poly-blend is literally just plastic. People are basically paying twenty bucks to wear recycled soda bottles. I was reading this thing about microplastics in the ocean and how every time you wash those shirts, thousands of tiny plastic fibers just wash right down the drain and into the water supply. It really makes you wonder what we're drinking, you know? Like, is my tap water just dissolved t-shirts? I actually bought a water filter for my apartment, one of those heavy-duty ones that attaches right to the kitchen faucet, but it took me like three hours to install because the threading on my sink was completely stripped. I had to go to the hardware store twice just to get the right adapter. 

But anyway... yeah, it's been about ten months since all that started.

Over these past ten months, have you also had a period where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or irritable—needing much less sleep than usual—that happened around the same time as these suspicions and the voice?

Yeah, actually. There was this stretch... I don't know, maybe a few weeks? Where I just felt... incredible. Untouchable, really. I was barely sleeping, maybe two or three hours a night, and I had so much energy. I was talking nonstop to everyone at the warehouse about the new sneaker trends, like how the chunky soles are coming back but with these weird neon accents that honestly clash with everything. I actually bought a pair of those neon ones online, but they got lost in the mail. The tracking number just stopped updating in Omaha. Who even goes to Omaha? I think it's mostly cornfields and insurance companies. My uncle used to sell life insurance, but he quit because he hated wearing ties. 

But anyway, yeah, during those weeks when I was feeling so wired and talking a mile a minute, that's when I was also totally convinced the vendors were messing with my numbers. And that's when the voice was there, too, just kind of... pushing me, telling me I needed to move faster, work faster. It was all happening at the same time.

Outside of that few-week period when you were feeling wired and energetic, during the rest of these ten months when your mood was more normal, did the suspicious thoughts about coworkers and the voice continue?

Yeah, um... actually, yes. Even during a calmer stretch when I was sleeping more normally and not feeling like I was running the whole market, I still spent a few weeks believing people were tracking my buys. And I was still hearing the voice, especially back in the stockroom. 

The stockroom is always freezing, by the way. They keep the thermostat locked behind this little clear plastic box. I actually watched a video on how to pick those locks with a paperclip because I was so cold, but I never actually tried it. Did you know you lose most of your body heat through your head? I saw this guy on YouTube testing it with a thermal camera. He went out in the snow in just a swimsuit and a winter hat. He looked completely ridiculous, honestly, but the thermal camera was super cool. You can buy those cameras as attachments for your phone now. I thought about getting one to see if there were drafts in my apartment, because my heating bill was insane last month. Like, almost two hundred dollars for a one-bedroom. I should probably just buy weather stripping for the windows, but the hardware store is always so crowded on weekends. 

But... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, yeah. So even when my mood was totally normal and I was sleeping fine, the tracking stuff and the voice in the stockroom were definitely still happening for a few weeks.

Out of the full ten months, roughly how many weeks in total have you had the suspicious thoughts and voice while your mood was completely normal, compared to the time when you were in that energetic, wired stretch?

Um, so... looking back at the whole ten months, I'd say the vast majority of it was taken up by those wired, irritable stretches. Like, most of the time I was just overworking, feeling totally overconfident, and it was super hard for anyone to slow me down. The calmer periods where my mood was normal were actually pretty short in comparison. 

Which is wild, because when you're in it, time feels totally different. Kind of like when you're waiting in line at the DMV. I had to go last month to renew my registration, and I swear I was sitting in those hard plastic chairs for a year. The guy next to me was doing a crossword puzzle, but he was using a pen. Who does a crossword in pen? You have to be so confident. Or just reckless. My grandpa used to do them in pen, but he was a high school English teacher, so I guess he earned the right. He actually taught at the same high school I went to, which was always kind of weird because all the older teachers remembered him and would ask me how he was doing. It's a lot of pressure, honestly, having a family legacy at a public high school in the suburbs. 

But yeah, anyway, the normal mood parts were definitely just short little breaks compared to all the time I spent feeling wired and unstoppable.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports a 10-month history of persistent paranoid delusions (belief that coworkers/vendors are sabotaging him) and auditory hallucinations (a voice commanding him to work faster). These psychotic symptoms co-occurred with a distinct several-week manic episode (decreased need for sleep, elevated/expansive mood, grandiosity, pressured/tangential speech, increased goal-directed activity). Critically, the patient confirms that psychotic symptoms (delusions and hallucinations) persisted for several weeks during a period when mood was clearly euthymic/normal, satisfying the requirement for psychotic symptoms in the absence of mood episode for at least 2 weeks. Because mood episode symptoms were present for the majority of the active illness duration and psychotic symptoms occurred both during and independent of the mood episode, this pattern fits Schizoaffective Disorder rather than Bipolar Disorder with psychotic features (which would require psychosis only during mood episodes) or Schizophrenia (which would require mood symptoms to be brief relative to total psychotic duration). Tangential, circumstantial speech noted throughout also suggests formal thought disorder consistent with a primary psychotic-spectrum illness rather than pure mood disorder.
